Subtracting the mass of a proton (1.0073 Da) gives an estimated neutral molecular mass of ~182.038 Da. This mass is consistent with a molecular formula such as C₉H₁₀O₄ (exact monoisotopic mass 182.0579 Da) or C₁₀H₁₄O₃ (exact monoisotopic mass 182.0943 Da). To pinpoint the exact structure efficiently, we can retrieve the ¹H NMR spectrum of the sample, which will reveal characteristic chemical‑shift patterns (e.g., aromatic protons, carbonyl‑adjacent methylenes, etc.). Matching those patterns to simulated spectra of candidate isomers will let us identify the correct SMILES without exhaustive searching. Therefore, the next step is to obtain the proton NMR spectrum for the sample.</thought>
